b2021-1.ask: Which solid can be built from 2 white and 4 gray bricks?
steps: Count the bricks: 2 white and 4 gray. Every brick is the same size.
Check each solid: count how many white bricks and gray bricks it would need, looking at every visible face.
Cross out any solid that needs more than 2 white or more than 4 gray, or has a colour pattern a single brick can't make.
Only solid D works.
b2021-1.check: In D you can point to exactly 2 white bricks and 4 gray ones. ✓
b2021-1.spot: Building with a fixed set of pieces? Count each colour you need.
b2021-1.oops: Counting faces instead of bricks. One brick shows on several faces.

b2021-2.ask: Children hold hands in a row. In how many places are two children holding LEFT hands?
steps: Look at which children face you and which face away.
Two children facing the same way hold one left hand and one right hand.
Left hands meet only where a child facing you is next to a child facing away, in the right order.
Checking each pair in the picture, this happens in just 1 place.
b2021-2.check: Hold hands with a friend facing the other way and see which hands meet. ✓
b2021-2.spot: Left and right with people facing different ways? Act it out.
b2021-2.oops: Using your own left and right instead of each child's.

b2021-3.ask: A line through a grid of digits 1 to 9 makes a number (read in order from the star). Which line makes the biggest number?
steps: More digits make a bigger number, so first check which lines pass the most digits.
Among lines with the same number of digits, the biggest first digit wins.
The best lines start 9, 8 ... Compare them digit by digit.
Line E makes the biggest number.
b2021-3.check: Write each line's number and compare: E is biggest. ✓
b2021-3.spot: Biggest number? First the number of digits, then the first digit, then the next.
b2021-3.oops: Starting from the wrong end of the line. Always begin at the star.

b2021-4.ask: Sofie spells KENGU taking one letter from each box. Which letter must come from box 4?
steps: Box 3 only has N. So N comes from box 3.
K is only in box 2. So K comes from box 2.
G is in box 2 and box 4. Box 2 is used, so G comes from box 4.
Then E and U come from boxes 1 and 5.
b2021-4.check: Box 1 E, box 2 K, box 3 N, box 4 G, box 5 U: KENGU. ✓
b2021-4.spot: Matching puzzles? Start with the box or letter that has only one choice.
b2021-4.oops: Taking two letters from one box.

b2021-5.ask: Five puzzle pieces with 2, 0, 2, 1 and + fit into a rectangle. What's the answer to the calculation?
steps: Each piece has tabs and holes. Neighbouring pieces must fit: tab into hole.
The two end pieces must have flat outer edges.
Try orders until all tabs fit: the only fit spells 20 + 12.
b2021-5.check: Every tab fits a hole and both ends are flat. ✓
b2021-5.spot: Fitting pieces in a row? Find the end pieces first.
b2021-5.oops: Reading the pieces in the order they're drawn.

b2021-6.ask: A measuring tape wraps around a cylinder. What number is at the question mark?
steps: Look at how much the numbers go up from one loop to the one above.
The number directly above another is 21 more each time around.
Find a number below the question mark and add 21 for each loop up.
That gives 69.
b2021-6.check: Go up from the bottom loop: +21, +21 lands on 69. ✓
b2021-6.spot: Things that wrap around? Find how much one full turn adds.
b2021-6.oops: Counting along the tape one number at a time.

b2021-7.ask: Five shapes can only slide in the directions shown. Which one can get out through gate G?
steps: Gate G is a fixed width. A shape can only get through if it's narrow enough in every row.
Check how each shape can slide: some can only go sideways, some only up and down.
A shape must reach the gate AND fit through it.
Only shape B can do both.
b2021-7.check: Slide B along its arrows: it reaches G and fits. ✓
b2021-7.spot: Sliding puzzles? Check both: can it reach, and does it fit?
b2021-7.oops: Picking a shape that fits but can't move toward the gate.

b2021-8.ask: Which green-and-white paint mix is darkest?
steps: Turn each mix into 'green : white' in simplest form.
They're all the same mix, just bigger amounts.
So they're all equally dark.
b2021-8.answer: They will all be equally dark (E).
b2021-8.check: In each mix, green is exactly 1/4 of the paint. ✓
b2021-8.spot: Comparing mixes? Simplify each ratio first.
b2021-8.oops: Thinking more green paint makes it darker, even with more white too.

b2021-9.ask: Paper folded in half twice makes a small right triangle. Which shapes (P rectangle, Q square, R triangle) could the original be?
steps: Unfold the triangle step by step. Each unfold doubles it, mirroring across a fold line.
Depending on which edge you fold along, you can get different shapes.
Try it for each: you can unfold into a rectangle, into a square, and into a big triangle.
So any of P, Q or R works.
b2021-9.answer: Any of P, Q or R (E).
b2021-9.check: Fold a paper rectangle, a square and a triangle in half twice each: all can make the small triangle. ✓
b2021-9.spot: Unfolding? Try mirroring across different edges.
b2021-9.oops: Only trying one way to unfold.

b2021-10.ask: Lines are drawn in a square from corners and midpoints. Which coloured piece is 1/8 of the square?
steps: Midpoints cut things in half. Find pieces that are halves of quarters.
A line from a corner through the middle cuts the square into halves and quarters.
Check each coloured piece: what fraction of the square is it?
Piece D is exactly half of a quarter = 1/8.
b2021-10.check: 8 copies of piece D would cover the whole square. ✓
b2021-10.spot: Fractions of a square? Split it into halves, then quarters, then eighths.
b2021-10.oops: Picking by how small the piece looks.

b2021-11.ask: Cut the strip 5021972970 twice to make 3 numbers. What's the smallest sum?
steps: 10 digits into 3 numbers: best lengths are 4, 3 and 3 (one long number).
The 4-digit number matters most, so make it start with the smallest digit: 1.
b2021-11.check: Other cuts make a bigger 4-digit number, like 5021 + 972 + 970 = 6963. ✓
b2021-11.spot: Smallest sum after cutting? Keep the longest number as small as possible.

b2021-12.ask: Tours from A, B and C (each going round part of the map) are 10, 12 and 13 km. The inner loop Zoo–Park–Port is 15 km. How long is the tour A → B → C → A?
steps: Add the three tours: 10 + 12 + 13 = 35 km.
Together they cover the outer route A–B–C–A once AND the inner loop once.
So 35 = outer route + 15.
Outer route = 35 − 15 = 20 km.
b2021-12.spot: Several overlapping routes? Add them all, then take away what's counted extra.

b2021-13.ask: Which piece in the middle would NOT let Rosa follow the line from one arrow to the other? (Pieces can turn.)
steps: The path enters the middle square from one side and must leave from another.
For each piece, try turning it four ways: does any turn connect the right two sides?
Pieces A, B, C and E all have a turn that connects them.
Piece D never connects the two ends, however you turn it.
b2021-13.check: Trace the full path with each piece: only D breaks it. ✓
b2021-13.spot: Which piece can't work? Try all four turns of each one.
b2021-13.oops: Only trying each piece one way up.

b2021-14.ask: Three hexagons share corners. Each hexagon's six corners add to 30. Some numbers are hidden. What's at the question mark?
steps: Left hexagon: the known corners add to 12, so its two hidden corners add to 18.
Right hexagon: the known corners add to 23, so its two hidden corners add to 7.
The top hexagon includes those hidden corners, the question mark and 1.
b2021-14.spot: Shapes sharing corners? Find the hidden pairs' totals, not each number.
b2021-14.oops: Trying to find each hidden number separately.

b2021-15.ask: Three rectangles of the same height have areas 12, 18 and 22. AB = 6 cm covers the first two. How long is CD?
steps: AB covers the 12 and 18 rectangles: area 30 with width 6.
So the height is 30 ÷ 6 = 5 cm.
CD covers the 18 and 22 rectangles: area 40.
b2021-15.spot: Rectangles with the same height? Area ÷ height = width.
b2021-15.oops: Guessing from how wide they look.

b2021-16.ask: A pyramid of 10 balls has letters A to E, two of each. Three side views are shown. What letter is on the hidden ball?
steps: The top ball is A in every view: that's one A.
There are two As. Look at all the balls you can see in the three views: the second A never appears.
So the second A must be the ball that's hidden from every side.
That's the question mark ball.
b2021-16.check: Count each letter across the views: B, C, D and E each appear twice; only one A shows. ✓
b2021-16.spot: Hidden pieces? Count what you can see and find what's missing.
b2021-16.oops: Counting the top ball as two balls because it shows in every view.

b2021-17.ask: Ronja (white tokens) and Wanja (gray tokens) take turns placing tokens on two piles. Ronja goes first. Which pair of piles couldn't happen?
steps: They alternate: white, gray, white, gray... 8 tokens in total.
So the very last token placed is gray (Wanja's).
The last token placed must be on top of one of the piles.
In picture E, neither pile has gray on top. That can't happen.
b2021-17.check: In every other picture, at least one pile has a gray token on top. ✓
b2021-17.spot: Taking turns? Think about who goes last.

b2021-18.ask: The lock started on the right code. Every wheel was turned the same amount the same way, and now it shows 6348. Which can't be the code?
steps: If every wheel turns the same amount, each digit changes by the same step (and 9 wraps around to 0).
Compare 6348 with each choice, digit by digit.
8560: each digit is 2 more (6→8, 3→5, 4→6, 8→0) ✓. 3015: each is 7 more ✓.
4906: 6→4 is +8 but 3→9 is +6. Not the same. Impossible.
b2021-18.spot: Everything shifted by the same amount? Check that every digit moved the same.
b2021-18.oops: Forgetting digits wrap around from 9 to 0.

b2021-19.ask: 20 apples and 20 pears. Carl takes 20 fruits and Luca gets the rest. Which statement is always true?
steps: Carl's apples + Carl's pears = 20.
Carl's apples + Luca's apples = 20 (all the apples).
Compare: both have Carl's apples. So Carl's pears = Luca's apples.
b2021-19.answer: D: Carl got as many pears as Luca got apples.
b2021-19.check: Example: Carl 12 apples, 8 pears. Luca 8 apples, 12 pears. Carl's pears 8 = Luca's apples 8. ✓
b2021-19.spot: Two totals sharing a part? Take away what they share.
b2021-19.oops: Picking B. Carl might get 15 apples and 5 pears.

b2021-20.ask: One train leaves X (180 min to Y), another leaves Y (60 min to X), at the same time on a single track. Where should the double track go so they can pass?
steps: The X train covers 1/180 of the track per minute, the Y train 1/60 = 3/180. Together 4/180 per minute.
They meet when together they've covered the whole track: 180 ÷ 4 = 45 minutes.
In 45 minutes the X train has gone 45/180 = 1/4 of the way.
The track has 6 sections, so they meet 1.5 sections from X: in the second section. That's B.
b2021-20.check: The Y train went 3/4 of the way in 45 minutes: 45 ÷ 60 = 3/4. ✓
b2021-20.spot: Two things meeting? Add their speeds and find when they meet.
b2021-20.oops: Putting the double track in the middle.

b2021-21.ask: Five people around a round table. Ann isn't next to Bob. Dan is next to Ed. Bob isn't next to Dan. Who sits next to Carina?
steps: Bob has two neighbours. Not Ann, not Dan. So Bob sits between Carina and Ed.
Dan is next to Ed. So around the table: Carina, Bob, Ed, Dan, and Ann fills the last seat.
Ann sits between Dan and Carina.
Carina's neighbours: Bob and Ann.
b2021-21.check: Circle: Carina, Bob, Ed, Dan, Ann. Every rule holds. ✓
b2021-21.spot: Seating puzzles? Start with the person who has the most 'not next to' rules.
b2021-21.oops: Forgetting the table is round, so the ends are neighbours.

b2021-22.ask: A recipe for 100 pancakes uses 25 eggs, 5 kg flour, 4 l milk, 1 kg butter. Maurice has 6 eggs, 400 g flour, 0.5 l milk, 200 g butter. Most pancakes?
steps: Work out how many pancakes each ingredient alone could make.
Eggs: 25 eggs make 100, so 1 egg makes 4. 6 eggs → 24 pancakes.
Flour: 5000 g makes 100, so 50 g makes 1. 400 g → 8 pancakes. Milk: 0.5 l → 12.5. Butter: 200 g → 20.
The flour runs out first: 8 pancakes.
b2021-22.check: 8 pancakes need 2 eggs, 400 g flour, 0.32 l milk, 80 g butter. All enough. ✓
b2021-22.spot: Several ingredients? The one that runs out first decides.
b2021-22.oops: Using the eggs or milk and forgetting to check the flour.

b2021-23.ask: Three gears each have a black tooth. The small gear turns once clockwise. Where are the black teeth now?
steps: Touching gears move the same number of teeth, but turn in opposite directions.
The small gear turns once: it moves all its teeth. Count them.
Each bigger gear moves that many teeth, which is only part of a turn. Its neighbour turns the other way.
Move each black tooth that many teeth in the right direction: picture A.
b2021-23.check: Count teeth moved on each gear in A: they match the small gear's teeth. ✓
b2021-23.spot: Gears? Count teeth, and remember neighbours turn the opposite way.
b2021-23.oops: Turning every gear one full turn.

b2021-24.ask: Apple + orange = pear + peach. Apple + pear < orange + peach. Pear + orange < apple + peach. Which fruit is heaviest?
steps: From the first fact, the pairs (apple, orange) and (pear, peach) balance.
Compare 'apple + pear < orange + peach' with the balance: take it apart and you find pear < orange.
Compare 'pear + orange < apple + peach' the same way: pear < apple.
Then in the balance, peach must be bigger than both apple and orange to make up for the light pear. So peach is heaviest.
b2021-24.check: Example: apple 3, orange 4, pear 2, peach 5. 3 + 4 = 2 + 5 ✓, 3 + 2 < 4 + 5 ✓, 2 + 4 < 3 + 5 ✓. Peach biggest. ✓
b2021-24.spot: Balances and 'less than'? Combine the facts and cancel what's the same.

b2021-25.ask: Fewest squares to colour so the 6 × 6 grid has four lines of symmetry (across, up, and both diagonals)?
steps: Four lines of symmetry means every coloured square has copies mirrored across all four lines.
Each of the 3 coloured squares gets copied to up to 8 positions.
Mark all the copies of each coloured square on the grid.
Counting new squares needed: 21.
b2021-25.check: Fold the finished grid along any of the four lines: both halves match. ✓
b2021-25.spot: Lots of symmetry? Copy each piece to all its mirror spots.

b2021-26.ask: Three pirates each answered one question truthfully and lied about the other. What's Graybeard's total of coins and diamonds?
steps: Pirates 2 and 3 both say 7 coins. If both lied about coins, both told the truth about diamonds, but they say 4 and 7. Impossible.
So 7 coins is true. Pirates 2 and 3 told the truth about coins, so they lied about diamonds.
Pirate 1 said 8 coins, a lie. So pirate 1 told the truth about diamonds: 6.
7 coins + 6 diamonds = 13.
b2021-26.check: Pirate 1: coins wrong, diamonds right. Pirates 2, 3: coins right, diamonds wrong. ✓
b2021-26.spot: Half-truth puzzles? Look where two people agree.
b2021-26.oops: Assuming the pirate who differs is the liar on everything.

b2021-27.ask: Each shelf holds 64 dl of juice in large, medium and small bottles. How much does a medium bottle hold?
steps: Write each shelf as a sum: (bottles) = 64.
Compare shelves: if one shelf has twice as many of some bottles, halve it to compare with another.
Taking away what two shelves share leaves an equation with just one or two kinds of bottle.
Solving step by step, a medium bottle holds 10 dl.
b2021-27.check: Put the sizes back on every shelf: each totals 64 dl. ✓
b2021-27.spot: Shelves with the same total? Compare them and cancel what's the same.
b2021-27.oops: Trying to guess all three sizes at once.

b2021-28.ask: A 7 × 7 × 7 cube has both diagonals drawn on each face. How many small cubes have a red line on them?
steps: On one face, the two diagonals each pass through 7 small squares, sharing the middle one: 7 + 7 − 1 = 13.
But each corner cube is on 3 faces' diagonals, so it was counted 3 times instead of once.
8 corners × 2 extra counts = 16. 78 − 16 = 62.
b2021-28.check: Only corners are shared between faces' diagonals, and we fixed them. ✓
b2021-28.spot: Counting on a cube's faces? Watch for corners and edges counted more than once.

b2021-29.ask: 10 elves and trolls hold tokens 1 to 10. Each says a number from 1 to 10. Trolls lie, elves tell the truth. The answers add to 36. Fewest trolls?
steps: The real numbers add to 1 + 2 + ... + 10 = 55.
The answers add to 36, so lies must lower the total by 19.
The biggest lie lowers it most: the troll with 10 says 1 (−9), with 9 says 1 (−8). Two trolls: at most −17. Not enough.
Three trolls can lower it by 19 or more (e.g. 10 says 1, 9 says 1, 8 says 6). So at least 3.
b2021-29.spot: Fewest people needed? Let each one do as much as possible.
b2021-29.oops: Forgetting the answers must be from 1 to 10 (no 0).

b2021-30.ask: Cards have four shapes in a 2 × 2 grid. Cards can sit side by side only if matching shapes touch. Which card was definitely NOT used?
steps: Look at the first card in the corner: circle and triangle are on top, star and square below.
Matching edges mean neighbouring cards keep the same shapes in the same row.
So in every card in the rectangle, circle and triangle stay together in one row.
Card E has circle and triangle in different rows. It can't be used.
b2021-30.check: All the other cards keep circle and triangle in the same row. ✓
b2021-30.spot: Rules about neighbours? Look for something that never changes.
b2021-30.oops: Checking only whether a card fits next to the first one.
